issues.description: Critical syntax error in getUserSubscription function - incomplete code with orphaned statement 'rows[0];' without variable declaration, making function non-executable
issues.suggestion: Complete the implementation: add 'const query = ...' and 'const rows = await db.query(...)' before line 189, and ensure 'row' variable is properly defined from rows[0]

issues.description: PCI-DSS violation: PaymentDetails interface accepts full credit card numbers (16 digits) and CVV in plain text, significantly expanding compliance scope and creating security risks even though only last 4 digits are stored
issues.suggestion: Never handle raw card data. Use payment gateway tokenization (Stripe, PayPal). Replace cardNumber and cvv with paymentToken: string to accept pre-tokenized payment methods from a PCI-compliant gateway

issues.description: CVV exposure in PaymentDetails interface violates PCI-DSS requirements - CVV must never be stored, logged, or passed through application code
issues.suggestion: Remove CVV from interface entirely. Submit CVV directly to payment gateway client-side, use tokenized payment processing where gateway handles CVV validation

issues.description: Missing null check in hasFeatureAccess - if db.query returns null/undefined, 'rows.length' will throw runtime error. Also missing validation for subscription.features being null or malformed JSON
issues.suggestion: Add comprehensive null checks: 'if (!rows || rows.length === 0) return false;' and 'if (!subscription?.features) return false;'. Wrap JSON.parse in try-catch and validate parsed result is string array

issues.description: Unsafe JSON.parse without error handling (lines 151, 181, 194) - malformed JSON in database will crash application. No type guard to ensure result is string array
issues.suggestion: Create parseFeatures helper function with try-catch: 'try { const parsed = JSON.parse(jsonString); return Array.isArray(parsed) && parsed.every(f => typeof f === 'string') ? parsed : []; } catch { return []; }'

issues.description: No transaction management in processPremiumPayment - chargeCard (line 50) and upgradeUserSubscription (line 56) execute as separate operations. If subscription upgrade fails after charging card, user is charged without receiving subscription
issues.suggestion: Wrap operations in database transaction: 'await client.query('BEGIN')' before chargeCard, 'await client.query('COMMIT')' after success, 'await client.query('ROLLBACK')' on any failure

issues.description: Insufficient input validation in processPremiumPayment - userId parameter not validated for empty string, null, or malformed values. No verification that userId exists or belongs to authenticated user
issues.suggestion: Add validation: 'if (!userId || typeof userId !== 'string' || userId.trim().length === 0) throw new Error('Invalid user ID');' Add authentication/authorization checks

issues.description: Console error logging in chargeCard may leak sensitive payment data if error object contains transaction details or card information
issues.suggestion: Sanitize error logging: 'console.error('Payment processing failed for user transaction');' without error details. Log to secure audit system for compliance without sensitive data

issues.description: All db.query() calls (lines 124, 147, 173, 190) return untyped results (implicitly any), bypassing TypeScript type safety. Schema changes or unexpected data will cause runtime errors
issues.suggestion: Define typed interfaces for database results (PaymentRow, SubscriptionRow) and use generic type parameter: 'const rows = await db.query<SubscriptionRow>(query, [userId]);'

issues.description: Race condition in date comparisons - multiple 'new Date()' calls (lines 90-91, 177-179) may produce different times if execution is slow or clock skew occurs, causing inconsistent behavior near expiry times
issues.suggestion: Capture current time once at function start: 'const now = new Date();' then use 'now' for all comparisons within that function

issues.description: Incorrect expiry date validation - creates date with beginning of expiry month, but cards are valid through end of month. Card expiring '12/25' incorrectly treated as expired on December 1st
issues.suggestion: Set to last day of expiry month: 'const expiryDateObj = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month), 0);' (day 0 = last day of previous month, so month without -1)

issues.description: Magic numbers in validation - card number length (16), CVV lengths (3, 4) hardcoded without explanation. Tax rate (8%) and processing fee (2.9%) also hardcoded
issues.suggestion: Extract to named constants: 'const CARD_NUMBER_LENGTH = 16; const CVV_LENGTH_AMEX = 4; const CVV_LENGTH_STANDARD = 3; const TAX_RATE = 0.08; const PROCESSING_FEE = 0.029;'

issues.description: Hardcoded tier-to-features mapping in upgradeUserSubscription - if tiers or features change, this manual logic must be updated, increasing maintenance burden
issues.suggestion: Extract to configuration object: 'const TIER_FEATURES = { premium: [...], enterprise: [...] } as const; const features = TIER_FEATURES[tier];'

issues.description: Generic error messages like 'Invalid payment details' don't indicate which specific validation failed, making debugging difficult for developers and unclear for users
issues.suggestion: Use specific error messages or typed error objects indicating exact validation failure (e.g., 'Card number must be 16 digits', 'Card has expired')

codeQuality.summary: Critical defects prevent safe deployment: fatal syntax error in getUserSubscription (line 189-195), severe PCI compliance violations handling raw card data and CVV, lack of transaction management risking financial integrity, and multiple high-severity type safety issues with unsafe JSON parsing and missing null checks. Requires substantial refactoring before production deployment.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Processes real payments and charges credit cards. Untested payment logic could result in financial losses, double-charging, failed transactions, data breaches, and PCI-DSS violations
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test successful payment processing with valid payment details, verify chargeCard and upgradeUserSubscription are called with correct parameters, assert return value is true

untestedPaths.reasoning: Card validation is first line of defense against fraud. Missing validation could allow processing invalid cards, accepting expired cards, bypassing CVV checks, and enabling financial fraud
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test rejection of: cards not exactly 16 digits, expired cards, invalid CVV lengths (not 3 or 4), malformed expiry dates. Assert 'Invalid payment details' error thrown

untestedPaths.reasoning: Without testing amount validation, system could accept partial payments or grant premium access without full payment, creating financial discrepancies
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test payment.amount < calculateSubscriptionPrice(tier) throws 'Insufficient payment amount'. Test exact amount and overpayment are accepted

untestedPaths.reasoning: Payment failures must be handled correctly to avoid charging customers without granting access or vice versa. Critical for financial integrity
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Mock db.query to reject with error, assert chargeCard returns false, verify subscription upgrade not called, verify getUserSubscription returns null

untestedPaths.reasoning: Determines feature authorization. Bugs could allow free users to access premium features (revenue loss) or block premium users from paid features (dissatisfaction)
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test returns true for valid subscription with feature, false for no subscription, false for expired subscription, false when subscription lacks requested feature

untestedPaths.reasoning: Incorrect pricing could undercharge (revenue loss) or overcharge customers (legal issues, chargebacks), creating accounting discrepancies
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test premium tier: base $9.99 + tax 8% ($0.80) + fee 2.9% ($0.29) = $10.84. Test enterprise tier: $49.99 + tax + fee = $54.44. Assert calculations accurate to 2 decimals

untestedPaths.reasoning: Subscription upgrades involve critical business logic for correct feature assignment, expiration dates, and database integrity via upsert
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test premium tier grants correct 3 features, enterprise grants 5 features, validUntil is one year from now (±1 second tolerance), query uses ON CONFLICT upsert

untestedPaths.reasoning: Affects user experience and billing. JSON parsing errors could crash application, missing subscriptions must be handled gracefully
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test returns Subscription object for existing user with correct userId/tier/validUntil/features, returns null for non-existent user, correctly parses JSON features array

untestedPaths.location: validatePaymentDetails() - expiry date edge cases lines 80-86
untestedPaths.reasoning: Date handling is error-prone with month boundaries, year offset calculations, and current month expiration edge cases
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test card expiring in current month is valid, card expired last month is invalid, December to January transition handled correctly (test 01/99 is valid)

untestedPaths.reasoning: Payment records critical for audit trails, compliance (PCI-DSS, SOX), customer support, and accounting reconciliation
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test stores only last 4 digits of card (not full number), records status as 'completed', logs error and returns false on database failure

untestedPaths.reasoning: Straightforward length check with clear pass/fail criteria, but important for input validation
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test accepts valid 16-digit cards from Visa/Mastercard/Discover, accepts 4-digit CVV for AMEX, accepts 3-digit CVV for others

untestedPaths.reasoning: Regex validation with clear patterns, important for user input handling
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: Test rejects invalid formats: month 13/00, missing leading zero (1/26), 4-digit year (12/2026), wrong separator (12-26), non-date strings. Test accepts valid MM/YY format

testCoverage.summary: Zero test coverage for critical payment and subscription module exposing severe financial, security, and operational risks. All 7 functions completely untested including payment processing, card validation, pricing calculation, feature authorization, and subscription management. 12 major untested paths identified across success flows, error conditions, edge cases, and security boundaries.

suggestions.location: Lines 99-102, 140-142 - configuration constants scattered across functions
suggestions.description: Extract hardcoded pricing configuration and feature mappings into centralized SUBSCRIPTION_CONFIG constant at module level
suggestions.benefits: Centralizes business configuration for easier updates, eliminates duplication of tax/fee rates and feature lists, makes values testable and mockable, improves maintainability when pricing or features change

suggestions.description: Introduce PriceBreakdown value object to encapsulate pricing logic and provide transparent price calculations
suggestions.benefits: Enables detailed price breakdowns for receipts/invoices, makes testing more granular (can verify each component), better transparency for users and debugging, follows Open/Closed Principle for easy extension with new fees

suggestions.location: Lines 189-196 - database row mapping in getUserSubscription
suggestions.description: Extract database row-to-domain object mapping into separate mapRowToSubscription function
suggestions.benefits: Separates data access from data transformation, makes mapping logic testable without database, easier to maintain as schema evolves, follows Single Responsibility Principle

suggestions.location: Lines 80-86 - expiry date validation in validatePaymentDetails
suggestions.description: Extract expiry date validation logic into separate isValidExpiryDate function
suggestions.benefits: Single Responsibility Principle - each function does one thing, easier to test expiry logic in isolation, improved readability with descriptive function name, simplified boolean logic

suggestions.description: Extract SQL queries into centralized SQL_QUERIES constant object
suggestions.benefits: Centralized query management for easier schema migrations, improved readability with multiline formatting, easier to audit and review SQL queries, reduces typo risk from query duplication

suggestions.description: Extract subscription expiry check into reusable isSubscriptionValid function
suggestions.benefits: DRY principle - eliminates duplicated validity check logic, testable in isolation, clear semantic meaning, reusable across multiple subscription checks

suggestions.location: Lines 164, 170 - multiple Date object creation in hasFeatureAccess
suggestions.description: Capture current time once at function start and add type annotation for parsed JSON
suggestions.benefits: Avoids creating multiple Date objects in comparisons, adds type annotation for parsed JSON, clearer intent with named variable, minor performance improvement

refactorings.summary: Identified 7 behavior-preserving refactoring opportunities focused on configuration management, function extraction, and design patterns. Highest priority: extract SUBSCRIPTION_CONFIG (eliminates duplication, centralizes business rules), introduce PriceBreakdown value object (improves transparency of critical payment logic), and extract database mapping (better separation of concerns). All refactorings improve maintainability, testability, and readability without changing external API.

recommendations.description: Fix fatal syntax error in getUserSubscription function (line 189) - incomplete code with orphaned statement makes function non-executable. Add missing query execution and variable declarations before deployment.

Redesign payment processing to never handle raw credit card data. Current implementation violates PCI-DSS by accepting full card numbers and CVV in application code. Implement payment gateway tokenization (Stripe, PayPal, etc.) where gateway handles sensitive card data and returns tokens for application use.

Implement database transaction management in processPremiumPayment to wrap chargeCard and upgradeUserSubscription operations. Current separate operations risk charging customers without granting subscriptions if upgrade fails after payment succeeds.

Add comprehensive test coverage for payment processing module (currently 0%). Critical paths requiring immediate tests: processPremiumPayment success/failure flows, validatePaymentDetails with all edge cases, chargeCard error handling, hasFeatureAccess authorization logic, calculateSubscriptionPrice accuracy, and upgradeUserSubscription business logic.

Add comprehensive error handling for JSON.parse operations (lines 151, 181, 194) and null checks for database query results. Create typed database result interfaces and use generic type parameters for db.query calls to enforce type safety throughout.

Fix expiry date validation logic (line 89) - cards are valid through end of expiry month, not beginning. Card expiring 12/25 should be valid through December 31, 2025. Also eliminate race conditions by capturing 'new Date()' once per function.

Add input validation for userId parameters in all public functions. Sanitize error logging to prevent sensitive payment data leakage in console output. Implement authentication/authorization checks before processing payments.

Refactor configuration management: extract SUBSCRIPTION_CONFIG constant consolidating pricing, tax rates, fees, and tier features. Extract SQL_QUERIES constant for centralized query management. This improves maintainability and reduces duplication.

Introduce PriceBreakdown value object to provide transparent price calculations with base/tax/fee components. Extract helper functions: isValidExpiryDate, isSubscriptionValid, mapRowToSubscription for better separation of concerns and testability.
